findings.problem: load_metrics has a pure-parsing signature (takes &str, returns Vec<Record>) but performs file I/O via fs::read_to_string on line 9. I/O is hidden inside what should be a calculation function.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot reason about side effects; function cannot be composed, tested deterministically, or used in contexts without a filesystem. Violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell.
findings.fix: Split into two functions: a shell function that performs fs::read_to_string and passes the string to a pure parse_metrics(&str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> calculation.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on Result panics on I/O error (permission denied, missing file, etc.).
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or hostile file paths cause process abort instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError> and use .map_err(|e| MetricError::Io(e)) or ? operator.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — stdout I/O inside parsing logic. This is a side effect fused into domain parsing.
findings.failure_mode: Parsing function produces observable side effects, making it non-deterministic from an external observer perspective and impossible to test without capturing stdout. Logging belongs in the shell, not the core.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If metrics/logging is needed, return a structured result that the shell can log.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on parse Result panics on invalid numeric input.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data (non-numeric value in second field) causes process abort instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|e| MetricError::Parse(field, e)) or similar typed error, then convert with checked u32->u16.

findings.problem: (...) as u16 — lossy narrowing cast from u32 to u16. Values >65535 silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: A value of 70000 becomes 4464 (70000 mod 65536). Data corruption with no warning, producing silently incorrect domain values.
findings.fix: Use u32::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| MetricError::Overflow(field))? and then u16::try_from().map_err(|_| MetricError::OutOfRange(field))?, or parse directly as u16: parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| MetricError::Parse(field, e)).

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec from split. If the line has no comma, parts has length 1 and parts[0] accesses a valid element but parts[1] on line 19 panics.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV lines (missing comma, empty lines) panic on index out of bounds rather than returning a typed error.
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and .ok_or(MetricError::InvalidLine)? to handle the single-separator grammar safely.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> — no domain cap on number of records; allocates for every line without validated capacity bounds. Also collects intermediate strings unnecessarily.
findings.failure_mode: A file with millions of lines exhausts memory. No try_reserve, no domain cap, no bounded resource policy enforced before allocation.
findings.fix: Validate an absolute domain cap (e.g., MAX_RECORDS) before allocation; call Vec::try_reserve(validated_cap).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation)?; use split_once to avoid per-field String allocations; prefer &str views where possible.

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String and pub value: u16 — raw primitives for domain concepts. No newtype for name (should be non-empty string), no newtype for value (should carry range semantics), no domain error type, no typestate.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal states are representable: empty names, negative values via conversion, unbounded value ranges. The domain invariants are not enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Define newtypes: struct MetricName(&'static str) or newtype with smart constructor; struct MetricValue(u16) with range validation; define enum MetricError { EmptyName, InvalidValue(ParseError), Overflow, Allocation, Io(io::Error) }.

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> with no error type. All failures (I/O, parse, overflow, allocation) are communicated through panic rather than typed errors.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot distinguish between a missing file, malformed data, or resource exhaustion. No retry strategy possible, no graceful degradation.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError> with a typed error enum covering Io, Parse, Overflow, Allocation, and InvalidLine variants.

findings.problem: No benchmark crate dependency or benchmark module exists. Performance claims (if any) cannot be validated.
findings.failure_mode: Performance regressions go undetected. No baseline to measure against for allocation patterns or throughput.
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar benchmark dependency with a benchmark for load_metrics/parsing throughput and allocation count.

findings.problem: No profiling evidence exists. The use of Vec<String> per field (allocating strings for every CSV field) may be unnecessary — split_once + &str would avoid allocations entirely for read paths.
findings.failure_mode: Unoptimized allocation pattern could be the actual bottleneck, but without profiler data the optimization target is guesswork.
findings.fix: Run cargo-flamegraph or similar to verify allocation hotspots before optimizing.

findings.problem: No test module exists. No command evidence that the crate compiles, lints clean, or passes tests.
findings.failure_mode: No proof that the code compiles, let alone behaves correctly. Cannot verify any invariant or behavior.
findings.fix: Add tests module with unit tests for parse_metrics covering valid input, malformed input, empty lines, and boundary values.

findings.problem: println! serves as ad-hoc metrics/logging fused into the parsing core. This is a second-ring concern (observability) leaking into the calculation layer.
findings.failure_mode: Metrics are unstructured (human-readable string), non-machine-parseable, and cannot be routed to proper observability backends (metrics, tracing, structured logging).
findings.fix: Remove println! and return structured data. Shell layer handles all observability via typed return values.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any stated performance claim
no profiler data exists to validate allocation patterns
no test module exists — no command evidence of compilation or behavior
no allocation evidence (allocations per record, total bytes) for load_metrics
no command-truth evidence (no CI gate, no test run output)
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. The code contains 9 blockers and 3 warnings across all Holzman v9 absolute laws: panic surfaces (unwrap), hidden I/O (fs::read_to_string + println!), unchecked indexing, lossy cast (u32 as u16), unbounded allocation, missing domain modeling, and absent error taxonomy. Without running cargo fmt/check/clippy/test, there is residual uncertainty about compilation state, but the semantic violations are independent of compile state and must be fixed before any promotion.
